label: a6-053-fs-convergent-subsequence-implies-bounded
tail:
I have reviewed the item and its dependencies. The refutation is mathematically correct: the constructed sequence is well defined, the odd-indexed subsequence is constant (hence converges to 1), and the even-indexed terms grow without bound (so the sequence is unbounded). All numbered proof steps are logically valid. The only defect is an inaccurate citation in the Facts & Assumptions block.

### FINDING 1 — NONFATAL — location: Facts & Assumptions block, [L4]
CLAIM AS WRITTEN: "Absolute value: |t| \ge t always, and |t| = t when t \ge 0 ([[lem-of-abs-value]])."
WHY IT FAILS: The quoted text of `lem-of-abs-value` does **not** state that |t| = t when t \ge 0. It gives other properties (|x| \ge 0, |x|=0 \iff x=0, -|x| \le x \le |x|, |-x|=|x|, |xy|=|x||y|, and |x|<c \iff -c<x<c) but nowhere the claimed equality. The citation attributes to the lemma a claim it does not make. (The proof step 3.2 uses this claim, but the step can be repaired by using only |t| \ge t — which is licensed by the same lemma — and the same chain of inequalities; hence the defect is nonfatal.)
WHAT WOULD FIX IT: Either replace the citation with `[[def-abs-value]]` (which likely defines the absolute value piecewise) or drop the equality claim and use only |y_{e_j}| \ge y_{e_j} in the proof.

0 fatal, 1 nonfatal
